text:
As Europe looks like a sinking ship, Bitcoin could be the lifeboat, not gold.

Peter Tchir on why investors want assets they can move easily as slowdown risks build

"I think the potential for economic slowdown is there. I think a bunch of things are rolling off, the AI spend, cheap stuff coming out of China. And to some degree, I think Europe's fracturing as well."

"I could see Bitcoin outperforming certainly gold in this sort of environment where people are like, okay, I want some sort of financial asset that I can move around. Because everything's falling apart a little bit in Europe."

"England's actually talking about trying to get back in. Like, why would anyone want to join that sinking ship right now?"

"I do think the risk of an economic slide is here. Markets aren't pricing that in. If that comes into play, we see much wider credit spreads, and I think that drags down equities far harder and Treasuries continue to rally."

name: Roger
zh_summary: (Reposted by @jam_croissant) @rdd147 claims Anthropic used a 2000 bubble style trick, paying expenses via $108B of convertible notes redeemable at IPO, likening it to dotcom firms paying suppliers with equity and vendor financing at Lucent, Cisco and Nortel.
en_summary: (Reposted by @jam_croissant) @rdd147 claims Anthropic used a 2000 bubble style trick, paying expenses via $108B of convertible notes redeemable at IPO, likening it to dotcom firms paying suppliers with equity and vendor financing at Lucent, Cisco and Nortel.
text:
Yikes. Anthropic just pulled the exact accounting trick that companies did in 2000 bubble for IPO.

They hid all their expenses via convertible notes redeemable at IPO. $108 billion worth.

Dotcom firms often paid suppliers, ad agencies, lawyers and even landlords with stock or equity to save cash. AOL swapped shares for services and ads (e.g., Homestore, DrKoop). Telecom suppliers like Lucent, Cisco and Nortel used vendor financing, sometimes with equity or warrants, to drive equipment sales.

ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS.

The open-weight models continue to be a threat as more enterprises are seeing the value in owning their AI for a significantly cheaper cost. Anthropic has outlined all these risks in the S1.

Regardless on if you are buying the IPO, it seems like there is enough cash they can raise to continue paying their bills and making sure the downstream value flows into most of the semis...if the market

text:
Anthropic has officially revealed in its IPO filing today that the company expects to spend up to $120.5 billion on @SpaceX SI compute through 2029.

• Monthly payments up to $3.1B, or $37.2B annually.
• SpaceX is expected to deliver all contracted computing capacity by Dec 2026.
• Anthropic (and SpaceX) can terminate the agreements with 90 days' notice after the initial contract periods end in early 2027.

Here's the exact wording directly from the filing: "Between May and October 2026, we entered into and amended several agreements with SpaceXAI to access compute powered by Nvidia GPUs. Under the SpaceXAI arrangements, we agreed to spend an aggregate of up to $120.5 billion over terms extending into 2029, consisting of approximately $3.1 billion in the aggregate per month once all capacity has been delivered, which we expect in December 2026, with different fees during capacity ramping periods. Following initial non-cancelable periods ending in January 2027 and March 2027 under the respective agreements, each agreement may be cancelled by either party upon 90 days’ advance written notice."

en_summary: @jsblokland says the Bureau of the Fiscal Service raised its US debt to GDP projection for 2099 from 535% to 576% in one year, and now sees 200% by 2048, two years earlier than before.
text:
In the second edition of my book The Great Rebalancing, I used figures from the U.S. Bureau of the Fiscal Service’s report An Unsustainable Fiscal Path, showing that U.S. debt-to-GDP would more than quintuple, from around 100% today to 535% by 2099.

Just one year later, the Bureau raised that projection to 576%. An increase of 41 percentage points. In just one year!

The Bureau now also expects U.S. debt-to-GDP to reach 200% by 2048. Two years earlier than previously projected.

2048! That's just over 20 years away, and U.S. debt could have doubled relative to GDP.

In my book, I explain what this means for the financial system, how our economies grow, and, more importantly, what this debt-driven system means for your savings, purchasing power and wealth.

You can find The Great Rebalancing on Amazon and at all major online bookstores.

text:
All seven Anthropic co-founders made the same pledge in today’s S-1.

“our co-founders have each pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in Anthropic to philanthropic causes.”

The company also moved 846,840,960 shares, “representing 5% of our fully diluted shares,” into its own Anthropic Public Benefit Fund.

And as the founders give shares away, “their voting control through the Founder LLC will remain unchanged.”
